prompt: Build SignalBus, a small event bus that stores Consumer lambdas under event names and replays them in registration order on emit, with clear and handlerCount alongside.
explanation: Because Consumer<String> is a functional interface, a lambda can be stored in a collection like any other object and invoked much later -- that is the whole idea behind callback registration. Map<String, List<Consumer<String>>> gives each event name its own ordered list, and computeIfAbsent creates that list exactly once on first use. Every read has to cope with a missing name, so returning 0 instead of dereferencing a null list is what keeps emit and handlerCount safe.
hints: handlers.computeIfAbsent(name, key -> new ArrayList<>()) hands you the list to add the handler to, creating it if needed.
In emit, fetch the list first and return 0 when it is null; otherwise loop and call handler.accept(payload).
Map.remove returns the value that was removed (or null), which is exactly what clear needs to count.
